title: Bound till the Thaw
logline: A smuggler-guide racing medicine to her brother's fever village is rope-bound by the mountain spirits to the warden captain sworn to hang her crew. On the rope, every lie costs body heat, so every true word between them is both an intimacy and evidence.
central_question: Will Meera get the medicine through to Ranu, and will Rohan arrest her?

heroine_belief.opening: The law is only ever a noose for people like us.
heroine_belief.changed: A law is a rope; it depends who ties it.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.goal: Pack the redbark and get her crew out of Kothi Shilak before the wardens arrive.
beats: Before dawn in the salt house, Meera counts twelve packets of redbark into oilcloth aloud. She notices the crown stamp scraped off the crate lids, shrugs and writes the packets into the count (C01).
In the count she records the lowland middleman's last delivery. Its token for the next drop is a single brass button, which she sews into the ledger's spine (C21).

Kiran's note, brought down by the last crew pair to cross back: grey cough in Ranu, Nimmi's tally of the sick, and 'Didi, come before the children go.' Meera remembers his black-rimmed left ear. He jokes about it and has never once named the crossing that took it (C02).

Jassi (40) names every goat while grumbling about the run, then volunteers. Bindu sings knot-counts over the red rope, eight arm-spans of wool from Lata's house. Meera's age, 29, comes up when Jassi teases her about ten winters of this.
A Taravan salt merchant pays double. Meera tells him it buys the widow Puja's son a free crossing next run. She does not say please.
At the village gate stand the Closing Law notice and the hanging tree, with two fresh pegs from last winter.
Warden horns sound. Meera hides the redbark in Bindu's wool bales.
Rohan walks into the salt house. He stops a warden from kicking a goat, asks for 'the guide Jassi' by name, and calls Meera 'Guide' when she answers for him.
chapters.reader_question_out: Why does the queen's warden captain want a guide over a closed pass in winter?
chapters.romance_change: The hunter she knew only by reputation turns out to be precise and controlled, a harder enemy than she prepared for, and he notices her before he knows who she is.

chapters.title: The Writ
chapters.goal: Secure a guide over Shilak and find the Salt Fox while he is here.
beats: Rohan (35) searches the salt house to the plank. He finds pass ropes but no contraband, and notices Meera counting his steps under her breath.

He shows the writ of passage in Queen Sarala's own hand and tells the village only 'crown business at the Snow Fair, twenty days.' In his interiority the reader learns about the lapis goat seal, Pritam's coup and the order to bring in the Salt Fox at the thaw.

He asks the village who froze an ear on the pass two winters ago. The warden record of Dilan's death notes blood and torn frozen skin on the ice. Meera answers that half this village has lost something to that pass (C03).
Jassi refuses to guide without 'his second.' Meera insists on coming. Rohan pairs himself with Jassi and Meera with his lieutenant, Varun.
Varun, fastidious, polishes a brand-new brass button on his coat and calls Rohan 'Captain-ji.' He says he has chosen the gully approach as the safer route (C04, C22).
At night Rohan pays the widow Puja's seizure fine from his own purse and tells her not to name him (C23). He sees Meera at the salt-house door watching him leave, and says nothing.
Before dawn he finds a grain of red powder on Bindu's wool. He rubs it between his fingers and pockets it without a word.
chapters.reader_question_out: He has found the redbark trace. Why hasn't he searched the bales?
chapters.romance_change: He sees her choose a killing pass for an old goat man, and respect starts against his judgement. She has now watched him do a kindness she cannot explain.

chapters.title: The Second Slide
chapters.goal: Get Jassi, the goats and the hidden redbark up the gully alive.
chapters.value_shift: a living crew -> alone with her enemy
beats: In the gully Meera reads wind-slab and dislikes Varun's route. Jassi tells her about his sister's apricot orchard and the goat Badami, who will retire with him.
Varun drops back to fix a pack strap. Meera hears a double crack, iron striking first and then the slope letting go (C05).
The avalanche hits. Jassi is gone. Rohan throws Meera into the lee of a boulder and takes the second slide across his own back.
They dig until dark and find Jassi dead, with Badami's bell in his fist. Meera takes the bell (C25). Varun's tracks are buried, and the redbark is safe in Meera's own pack.
Rohan, ribs cracked, says, 'Your mountain. Give the orders.' He obeys each one.

The approach is buried behind them and no one crosses alone. At the Shilak Cairn they tie the red rope on each other's wrists: 'Meera. Ranu.' 'Rohan. Garh Neshar.' Blue cairn-light lifts out of the stones.
He asks why Ranu. She gives her first free truth to her enemy: 'My brother is dying there.'
chapters.reader_question_out: What will the bond cost two people who are each other's hanging?
chapters.romance_change: She owes him her life, and he hands command to her. The enemies are bound by the mountain, not by choice.

chapters.title: Watch My Hands
chapters.goal: Learn the bond's rules and reassert the law.
beats: Meera teaches the rules precisely: the distance limit, lie-cold, and what is free. She demonstrates with a small lie, 'Jassi hated those goats.' Her fingertips whiten, and the grief under it shows.
Rohan takes a share of the load and finds the twelve packets. She says truthfully that they are medicine for Ranu, and that she will walk off the mountain before he takes them.
He states the law: seizure and the rope at the thaw. She answers: 'Then arrest me at the thaw, Captain. Today you carry half.'
He asks, 'Are you the Salt Fox?' She stays silent, which is free. He says, 'Silence is an answer, Guide. Watch my hands, and I will watch yours.' It is a threat (C20).
He carries six packets and tells himself it is evidence custody. The barrier is now explicit: aiding her is harbouring.
Meera bets him he can't stay silent for an hour. He does it with ease, and she is furious to lose.
At the waystone below the Long Saddle she raises a small cairn for Jassi. Rohan takes off his glove to place a stone.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can two truthful adversaries survive a law that makes every truth evidence?
chapters.romance_change: They agree terms as truthful adversaries. He chooses to carry contraband for her, and she sees him grieve a man he barely knew.

chapters.title: Two Brothers in Arms
chapters.goal: Shelter at the waystone and keep a hurt captain moving.
beats: On the waystone a weathered carving shows two hands bound by one rope. Rohan quotes the warden chronicle, 'two brothers in arms.' Meera says the crews tell it as a warden and a smuggler. Neither can prove their version (C06).
Rohan steps past the rope's length to check a pitch, and the cold hits them both at once. Meera hauls him back hand over hand and tells him his body is hers to keep alive until the thaw.
They make a dung fire. He says aloud that sharing it is harbouring, then sits down at it anyway.
She notices he breathes shallowly on his left side. He deflects.
First trade of questions. She asks what is at Garh Neshar, and he refuses. She asks why he hunts the crew, and he answers that a warden died on this pass two winters ago.
She asks again, flatly, whether his ribs are hurt. He says, 'It's nothing.' The waystone hums higher, and under the cairn-light she sees his fingertips start to whiten as he pulls his glove on.
chapters.reader_question_out: How big was that lie, and what will it cost him on the climb?
chapters.romance_change: Each learns the other's body is now their own survival. He deliberately commits his first harbouring at her fire.

chapters.title: Taking the Cold
chapters.goal: Hide his ribs and keep pace for the deadline.
beats: On the morning climb Meera asks outright whether his ribs are broken. He says, 'They are fine.' It is a middling lie, and frostnip creeps over his knuckles.
She strips her glove and says, 'Give me your hand.' He gives it, not knowing what she can do. The cold flows into her, and she knows the lie was middling.
He watches her hands go white and shake as she explains the loophole. She says, 'Now we go slow, and you tell me true, or I take it every time.'
He tells the truth: two ribs cracked. She binds them with Jassi's spare cord.
That night she shakes, and fire can't touch lie-cold. He gives her his pattu. She refuses it, then takes it.
He tallies her choice: she could have let him slow and fall behind. She paid instead.
She asks, 'Promise you won't lie again?' He knows a promise binds. 'No. I'll show you.'
chapters.reader_question_out: What will a man who won't promise do instead?
chapters.romance_change: She makes the first rational trust choice, paying for his lie in her own flesh. He resolves never to lie to her and refuses to dress it up as a promise.

chapters.title: Other Ropes
chapters.goal: Cross the first day of the Long Saddle before the weather.
beats: Glare and squeaking snow. Meera counts steps aloud. Rohan's eyes burn, so she cuts goggle slits in a strip of leather from his writ case.
She spots two bound pairs on her line far below. It is Asha's crew from the lower salt road, and Asha never crosses Shilak unless someone pays.
Rohan admits he carries something the regent's people would pay a lordship for. He won't say what, which is free.
To lose the pursuers she wants a hidden crew ledge. He asks her not to show him anything he would have to report. She shows him anyway, because time matters more.
Competence duet: he reads the pursuers' pace and kit like a soldier, and she reads the snow.
Mid-traverse on the ledge, a snow bridge gives under Rohan. The rope snaps taut, and Meera braces on her axe, saying, 'Don't you dare.' The chapter cuts with him hanging.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can she hold him, and what does saving him show Asha's crew?
chapters.romance_change: She risks a crew secret for him, and he asks her to protect herself from him. It is the first time each guards the other against their own side.

chapters.title: The Rope-Hut
chapters.goal: Reach the Rope-Hut alive.
chapters.value_shift: fear of losing him -> one shared fire
beats: Meera hauls him out with a crew pulley trick, calling the count. He climbs on her numbers with his ribs screaming. Afterwards they both laugh, badly.
The Rope-Hut has one chulha, one sleeping shelf and a juniper pile. Meera counts forty-one sticks.
He names the crime aloud: this fire is harbouring. She answers, 'Then hang yourself warm.'
Checking the redbark for damp, he rubs the powder and names it crown-grade, ground fine, with the store's sieve mark. She says truthfully that her middleman never told her (C07).
He cooks the sattu badly and she lets him. They negotiate the one shelf. He sleeps on the floor within the rope's length, and she lies awake listening to him breathe.
Far below on the Neshar side, torches climb the road. They are not Asha's. They are the regent's hunters.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who told the regent's hunters which pass to climb?
chapters.romance_change: The one fire becomes a shared crime. She lets him care for her in a small way, and she is now awake to his body.

chapters.title: Clean-Cut
chapters.goal: Decide whether to wait out the hunters or go down.
beats: Meera sets the firewood rule: one question each night, and each refused question burns one juniper stick. Evasion now costs warmth.
Her question: who died? He answers. Dilan, twenty-three, his youngest warden, died on this pass chasing a Kothi smuggler in a storm.
His question: who taught her the line? Her mother, who died of fever ten winters ago in a closed winter. Meera was nineteen.
She sleeps. Alone at the fire, he takes out Dilan's rope end and ties and unties the fibres. They are cut clean, not frayed (C08). He swore at the warden hall to find the smuggler on that rope.
She half-wakes, sees him put the rope away and doesn't ask. He notices that she chose silence.
He catches himself filing every truth she tells him as evidence, and hates it.
chapters.reader_question_out: Why does a rope that was cut clean keep him awake?
chapters.romance_change: They trade their first costly griefs. She gives him a free silence about his private ritual, and he begins to resent his own habit of building a case against her.

chapters.title: Parley
chapters.goal: Learn what Asha wants and keep her crew off them.
beats: Asha's two pairs camp above the hut. Asha (28) calls a parley from a rock rib, staying within her own rope.
Asha names her price. The regent will pay a lordship's purse and a crown pardon for 'the warden's coat and whatever's sewn in it' (C10).
Asha's tracker Lalit boasts of the gully approach: 'three wardens and two goat-folk.' Only the approach plan held those numbers, and Meera marks it (C09).
Meera offers salt-road favours. Asha laughs, prices her and swears an invented oath.
Inside, Meera asks directly what is in his coat. He refuses twice and burns two sticks, then gives part of the answer: 'The queen's will.'
His breath rattles. In the middle of telling her the hunters' road, he collapses. She catches him, and his skin is burning.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can she keep him alive, and what will she find on him?
chapters.romance_change: She learns that his coat is worth her crew's pardon. He pays wood for his secret but then gives her part of it, a first partial disclosure of his mission.

chapters.title: The Lapis Goat
chapters.goal: Break his lung fever.
chapters.value_shift: holding her enemy's life -> giving power back
beats: She strips his coat to poultice his ribs with juniper steam and spends a half-pinch of redbark on him. She records it in the count: Ranu is one dose poorer.
In the coat seam she finds the queen's seal, lapis cut with a mountain goat, on a cord tied in a warden's double hitch.
In fever he talks of Pritam, the Snow Fair and twenty days. She pieces together the coup, and why Asha wants the coat.
She holds the seal a long time. It could buy a pardon for her crew from Asha and medicine for Kiran.
She sews it back in and reties the cord in his double hitch, not her knot (C11).
He surfaces enough to see her finish the knot. Neither speaks.
In the count, under the half-pinch, she writes: 'One captain. Price: none.'
chapters.reader_question_out: Did he see enough to understand what she just refused?
chapters.romance_change: She could betray him for everything she wants and visibly doesn't. Trust becomes rational for him.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Knot
chapters.goal: Gather wood and watch Asha's crew.
chapters.value_shift: a profiteer in his eyes -> someone he can't fit into his picture
beats: Rohan is too weak to walk, and she can't go further than eight arm-spans. She drags him in his blankets to the door so she can reach the deadfall, and the comic logistics leave them both swearing.
Asha's pairs move off downslope and leave a tied-off food cache. Its knot is in an old pattern that matches the carved hands on the cairns (C12). Meera copies it into the count.
His question, lucid: why does she charge the rich double? So the poor cross free. He cannot make it fit any warden record.
Her question: has he hanged anyone? Two men, he says, and one was a boy carrying salt to his mother. He says it flatly, and his hands stay warm.
She doesn't forgive him. She counts it.
He says, 'The double price is in no record.' She answers, 'Nobody writes down what we do for free.'
chapters.reader_question_out: If the warden records are wrong about her, what else are they wrong about?
chapters.romance_change: His misjudgement of her as a profiteer breaks, and she hears his worst deed without a lie. The first reversal of judgement runs in both directions.

chapters.title: Hunters' Fires
chapters.goal: Get himself mobile and read the hunters.
beats: Rohan walks again, ashamed of having been dragged. Meera drills him on rope work until he stops apologising.
The hunters' fires are climbing Rohan's own fallback route, which only he and Varun drew. He notices and refuses the thought (C13).
Nineteen sticks of juniper and nine days to the Snow Fair. They must move within two days.
He asks about the Salt Fox again. She burns a stick rather than answer, and he sees she will pay for evasion.
She asks why he calls her 'Guide.' The crew name is a hanging name, he says, and he won't say it to her face. It is true.
His hand rests on the rope beside her wrist, and she doesn't move hers.
Lalit's voice rises from the slope below, calling directions. Asha's crew is guiding the regent's hunters.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who sold the route, and to whom?
chapters.romance_change: He admits his name for her is a protection, not a dismissal. She lets a touch stay, the first physical allowance either gives.

chapters.title: Died on the Pass
chapters.goal: Plan a way down past the hunters.
beats: Plan: the crew route called the Goat's Teeth avoids the hunters' road but costs a day, and the storm sky is building.
Her question: why keep the law? He answers that his grandfather 'died on the pass' when the Closing Law was new. He believes it was an accident, and he keeps the law so no one dies that way (C14).
His question: what would she do if the law were gone? 'Sleep.'
She asks whether he pays poor families' seizure fines, as the widow Puja said. He stays silent and burns a stick, and she knows he does (C23 payoff).
They nearly kiss. She pulls back with a new reason: 'At the thaw you deliver me. I don't kiss my noose.'
The storm wall rises over the Long Saddle.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can they get down the Goat's Teeth before the storm and the hunters close?
chapters.romance_change: She learns the source of his law and his secret mercy. Desire is named and refused for a new reason: the thaw delivery, not hatred.

chapters.title: The Goat's Teeth
chapters.goal: Break past the hunters down the Goat's Teeth.
beats: Two of the regent's hunters, bound as a pair, come up the Teeth. Rohan fights them in a disciplined way, disarming one and breaking the other's wrist rather than killing.
Meera reads a loaded slope and cuts a small slide that blocks the second pair. It is snow-craft, not magic.
In one hunter's purse Rohan finds a twist of crown-grade redbark with the same sieve mark as hers (C15).
The storm hits and forces them back up to the hut.
Meera's hands are raw with ordinary cold. He warms them against his skin, and this time fire and touch both work.
Eleven sticks left.
At the fire she starts, 'The redbark in my pack and that purse came from the same—' A gust tears the door open and scatters the woodpile into the dark. They must save it or freeze.
chapters.reader_question_out: What was she about to name, and can they last the night?
chapters.romance_change: They fight as one unit, each protecting the other in their own domain. His first deliberate skin-to-skin care is accepted.

chapters.title: What the Storm Kept
chapters.goal: Survive the storm night on the last of the wood.
beats: They save seven sticks for a full night of storm. Meera says the arithmetic aloud: no lies tonight, because they can't afford the heat.
'I am the Salt Fox.' Her hands stay warm. He answers, 'My writ orders me to deliver the Salt Fox to Taravan at the thaw.' His hands stay warm too.

They work it out together from the evidence: Varun's gully route, the double crack, Varun lagging, Lalit's numbers, the hunters on Varun's fallback, and crown redbark in a hunter's purse and in crates with scraped stamps. Varun set the avalanche, and he is her middleman.
The mirror: her lifeline was his enemy's purse, and she has been funding Pritam's coup. He trusted the man who killed Jassi.
Both are complicit, and every earlier chapter rereads.
The first kiss, costed: she is kissing the man who must deliver her. He promises, 'I will not let you fall on this mountain.' The rope hums.
She realises what that means. Until the thaw, his life is bound to her footing, and the thaw is when he must hand her over.
chapters.reader_question_out: What does a promise to keep her safe do to a man ordered to hand her to the rope?
chapters.romance_change: Full mutual confession of the two facts that make them enemies, then a first kiss chosen anyway. His promise turns care into a contract with the cold.

chapters.title: Below the Snowline
chapters.goal: Descend to Ranu past the hunters.
chapters.value_shift: a promise made -> the weight of it
beats: The storm clears. Rohan, newly bound by his promise, tries to make every step safe. She pushes back: 'Your promise doesn't make you my guide.' He learns that keeping it means obeying her.
He tells her truthfully that a warden cannot pardon. He can't unwrite her name; only the queen can.
He grieves Varun, ten years his friend, and lets the anger show.
Birch gives way to walnut slope, and they smell boiled walnut leaf and hear coughing behind timber walls.
On the slope he counts new graves in the frozen ground, many of them small. There are thirty-one.
Nimmi, with a shovel: 'Blockade dead. Thirty-one this winter. You're the captain who signs it?' He says, 'Yes.'
chapters.reader_question_out: What will Meera find in Nimmi's house, and what will Ranu do with a warden?
chapters.romance_change: As lovers they hit their first conflict: protection against her command. He chooses to protect her by deferring to her, and he faces his own victims at her side.

chapters.title: Twelve Packets
chapters.goal: Get redbark into Kiran and the worst of the children.
chapters.value_shift: the hope of arrival -> the grief of triage
beats: Kiran lies in Nimmi's house, grey and still joking: 'Didi, you brought a warden?'
Nimmi lists symptoms like grievances. Twelve packets less a half-pinch makes eighteen courses for forty sick.
Meera and Nimmi choose who gets a course, and Meera writes each name in the count. She won't let Rohan watch the choosing, and he holds the lamp anyway.
Rohan carries water house to house but can't go further than eight arm-spans from her, so he follows her everywhere.
Under Kiran's pillow Meera finds a tarnished warden's badge. He won't say whose it is (C16).
Sunni, seven, gets her course too late and dies before dawn.
chapters.reader_question_out: Whose badge is Kiran hiding, and can Meera forgive the count she made?
chapters.romance_change: He stays present for her worst work without judging or rescuing. She lets him witness it.

chapters.title: Nimmi's Count
chapters.goal: Bury Sunni, stretch the medicine and keep Rohan hidden.
chapters.value_shift: grief -> anger at the law and the man
beats: At the graveside Meera faces Rohan with the law. He argues that without the Closing Law the regent's grain wagons and the salt lords would own the passes. She answers that it kills children. Both are right.
The regent's patrol rides through Ranu and marks sick houses with ash 'for cleansing after the Fair' (C26).
Rohan must hide in the goat loft, and she must stay within the rope's length, so they lie pressed together in the hay.
In the loft he whispers the truth: he doesn't know if he can keep this law after Ranu.
The patrol captain says the general will ride up after the Snow Fair.
Back down, Meera finds she has stopped wanting him to be the villain.
chapters.reader_question_out: What does 'cleansing' mean, and how long does Ranu have?
chapters.romance_change: Their values collide in full, and he admits his certainty is cracking. She loses the comfort of hating him.

chapters.title: Across the Rope
chapters.goal: Get through the night after Sunni.
chapters.value_shift: enemies at peace -> lovers by choice
beats: In Nimmi's storehouse Meera writes Sunni's name in the count. He asks to see it, and she lets him.
The truth across the rope: 'I signed the Shilak blockade order three winters running. Sunni is in my hand too.' His hands stay warm. It is acknowledgement, not absolution.
She writes his name in the count beside the blockade line, the first time she has let him into her ledger.
The open-door scene follows, with both their ages (29 and 35) on the page and explicit consent: she asks, and he asks back what she wants. His ribs and her careful hands shape it.
What changes: she chooses the man who carries the noose with her eyes open, and he commits harbouring knowingly.
Afterwards he avoids anything that sounds like a promise, and she notices. She asks, 'Is this only the cold?' He says, 'No.' His hands stay warm.
Kiran's cough through the wall stops. She runs, and finds the fever has broken.
chapters.reader_question_out: Lovers now, so what happens when the thaw and his writ arrive?
chapters.romance_change: They become lovers by a choice made after a costly, verified truth. Desire is now also evidence, and she writes him into her ledger.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.goal: Plan the road to Garh Neshar for the Snow Fair, now six days off.
beats: Kiran is recovering and needles 'the warden wearing my sister's pattu.' When Rohan mentions Dilan, Kiran goes still and changes the subject. The reader sees it and Rohan does not.
Nimmi says a crown surveyor woman has been trapped at Garh Neshar since first snow. Rohan knows at once it is his sister Ila, and that she is in danger if Pritam wins.
Rohan must reach Garh Neshar, so the bond means Meera must come. She won't leave Ranu while children are on their last doses and the houses are marked with ash.
They argue strategy, not insults. He concedes three days, and she concedes she will walk the seal to the Fair.
He drafts his speech to the assembly and cannot write the line about the blockade.
He starts to tell Kiran that the smuggler on Dilan's rope— and Kiran sees Meera at the door and bolts.
chapters.reader_question_out: Why did Kiran run from that sentence?
chapters.romance_change: Their first conflict of goals as lovers is settled by negotiation between equals, each conceding something real.

chapters.title: The Badge
chapters.goal: Find out why Kiran ran.
beats: By the woodpile, within rope's length of Rohan inside, Kiran gives her the badge and won't speak the dead man's name. He was on the rope with Rohan's warden that night. The warden cut his own rope to stop Kiran being dragged off the ice, and Kiran's ear froze while he lay there (C02 payoff).
Kiran begs her. Rohan hunts the smuggler on that rope, and a death on an unlawful crossing hangs.
Meera's choice: telling Rohan forces him to report or break, while silence is free as long as he never asks.
She goes back inside. Rohan asks nothing, and she lies beside him awake.
The reader now knows seven chapters before Rohan does.
She realises there is exactly one question he could ask her that she can't survive.
chapters.reader_question_out: What will she do when he asks?
chapters.romance_change: For the first time she holds a secret that is about his own wound. Their intimacy now carries a clock.

chapters.title: Knots for Children
chapters.goal: Prepare to leave and find more redbark.
chapters.value_shift: closeness -> a distance he can feel
beats: Meera has turned careful and spare with words. He sees it and doesn't push, because silence is her right. It is a choice he makes.
He teaches Ranu's recovering children a warden's knot game, and Meera laughs for the first time since Sunni.
The redbark is down to its last doses. Nimmi says a masked buyer has paid crew contacts for medicine before.

He tells Meera he will petition the queen to strike the Salt Fox clause. He states it plainly as an intent and not a promise, because a promise he can't guarantee would freeze him. She understands it as care.
Alone, he writes to Ila.
A knotted cord appears at Nimmi's door: a crew signal to meet in the walnut grove tonight.
chapters.reader_question_out: Who is the buyer, and what does he want for the medicine?
chapters.romance_change: He respects her silence instead of interrogating it, and he offers his career against her writ. It is care offered through honest limits.

chapters.title: Cut-Corner Silver
chapters.goal: Get more redbark from the masked buyer.
beats: In the walnut grove Meera meets the buyer while Rohan waits behind a wall at the rope's full length.

The masked buyer is courtly, answers questions with questions and is gentle with Nimmi's grandson. He pays in Neshar silver stamped with a cut corner (C17) and hands over a sack of redbark from the regent's own stores.
He warns her that Varun crossed bound to a salt-road man. Varun is in Neshar with Asha and the regent's warrant for 'the seal-thief,' and will reach Ranu at dawn.
She asks his name. He asks why a smuggler wants names.
Back with Rohan: Kiran is too weak to flee and the new doses must be given. Rohan gives her the seal: 'Hide it where I can't lie about it.' She ties the cord in his double hitch (C11 payoff).
Horns sound on the road at dawn, and Varun's voice calls 'Captain-ji!'
chapters.reader_question_out: Will Rohan run or stand, and where has she hidden the seal?
chapters.romance_change: He hands her his mission entire. The man who carried the queen's will relies on the smuggler who once gave it back.

chapters.title: Captain-ji
chapters.goal: Protect Ranu, Meera and the seal.
beats: Varun arrives with the regent's men and Asha's pairs, carrying a warrant naming Rohan a seal-thief and traitor. Rohan surrenders to keep the soldiers out of the sick houses.
They search him and find no seal. Varun smiles, and the bounty becomes clear (C10 payoff).
Varun learns of the bond and keeps Meera chained near Rohan as 'the hired guide.' He doesn't know she is the Salt Fox.
Varun names Kiran in front of the village. His middleman's crew talk puts Kiran of Kothi on Dilan's rope: 'The smuggler who killed your boy has been sleeping in your sickhouse.'
Rohan looks at Meera, and she looks at nothing.
Asha watches the regent's men freshen the ash marks on Nimmi's house and goes quiet.
In the lockhouse, low, Rohan asks: 'Was Kiran on Dilan's rope?'
chapters.reader_question_out: Will she tell the truth that hangs her brother?
chapters.romance_change: Varun turns Rohan's grief into a weapon against their bond. For the first time Rohan asks her a question whose answer can destroy them.

chapters.title: No
chapters.goal: Save Kiran.
beats: Her calculation: silence is a yes to a man who cannot lie to the assembly. The truth hangs Kiran, and a lie costs flesh.
'No.' It is a great lie. Her left ring and little fingers die white inside her glove.
She keeps the hand in her lap under her pattu.
Rohan sees her shoulders shake. He could take her hand and know for certain, and he chooses not to reach.
She can't tell whether that was mercy or belief, and neither can the reader yet.
Outside, the guards talk of firing Ranu tonight to 'burn the cough' and its witnesses.
She can't feel her hand. She counts her breaths as her body cools.
chapters.reader_question_out: Will she live through the night, and will Ranu?
chapters.romance_change: She lies to him for the first time since the rope, paying her body for her brother. He chooses not to know, and that choice is itself the third trust beat.

chapters.title: Torches
chapters.goal: Keep her alive and stop the fire.
beats: Meera is sinking under shock and lie-cold. Rohan wraps her in his coat and pattu and keeps his body to her back, gloved, never touching her bare skin so he never takes the cold. He tells her truths all night to keep her awake: Dilan's laugh, Ila's measuring, his grandfather.
As she slips, his own fingertips begin to chill. His promise not to let her fall is pressing on him.
Through the slats he sees the regent's men circling the ash-marked houses with torches while the sick are inside (C26 payoff).
A grey-bearded officer rides up, looks at the houses and orders the torches lowered. The men obey, and Nimmi watches from her door (C18).
Rohan says aloud, 'Live, Guide. I won't ask you anything else.'
Before dawn Asha stands at the lockhouse door with a key and a knife: 'Price first.'
chapters.reader_question_out: What is Asha's price, and can Meera still walk?
chapters.romance_change: He keeps her alive while refusing to make her confess through her skin. He gives up the question for her life, and the promise binds his body to hers in the dark.

chapters.title: Asha's Price
chapters.goal: Escape with the seal and the evidence.
beats: Asha's price is not the pardon. She saw the torches, and she knows Varun's pardon is the same noose. She wants her crew alive and her name out of his books.

Meera tears a page from the count and trades it: the middleman's dates and crate marks, and the brass button token, which matches the new button on Varun's coat (C21, C22 payoff). Asha confirms that Varun paid her and that the middleman was his runner.
They escape, and Meera recovers the seal from the pot of steeping walnut leaf in Nimmi's chulha corner.
Nimmi looks at her hand. The fingers are dead and must come off after the Fair, or the rot will spread.
Rohan offers to carry her pack. For the first time she gives him her load.
Kiran insists on coming. Asha leads them on a salt-road path toward Garh Neshar.
Kiran says, 'Captain. I have to tell you what happened on that rope.'
chapters.reader_question_out: What will Rohan do with the truth Meera paid two fingers to hide?
chapters.romance_change: The competent one finally relies on him and lets him carry her load, a shift in her need made physical.

chapters.title: The Cut End
chapters.goal: Hear Kiran out.
beats: Kiran tells it without once saying Dilan's name. He calls him 'your warden' and 'him,' then hands over the badge (C16 payoff).
Rohan takes out the rope end. It is cut clean, and he has known for two winters that Dilan cut it himself and has never let himself say so (C03, C08 payoff).
Rohan understands her lie. He looks at her glove and knows its size. She says, 'Yes. I lied to you.'
In front of Asha, he declines to arrest Kiran. It is the first public bend.
Repair: Rohan names his part. He didn't reach because he was afraid of what he would have to do if he knew. She lied to protect her brother from him. He says, 'That's on my law, not your hand.'
They plan the Fair: he presses the seal, she gives evidence, and he speaks about the blockade.
Garh Neshar's brass bell hums in their teeth. It is the dawn of day twenty.
chapters.reader_question_out: Can a warden and a smuggler win a regent's assembly?
chapters.romance_change: Recognition: the lie is acknowledged and repaired with named responsibility on both sides, and his mercy to Kiran is chosen in full knowledge.

chapters.title: Watch My Hands
chapters.goal: Get the seal pressed and Varun exposed.
chapters.value_shift: outlaw -> witness in the record; lovers -> declared
beats: The Snow Fair ground: drums, roasting barley and a white sky. Pritam's investiture is under way, with Prince Kunal on the dais, Varun at Pritam's side and Ila in the crowd.
Rohan presses the seal. Its wax is mixed with the queen's own blood, proof she sealed it herself (C19). Pritam's claim is revoked.

Varun accuses Rohan. Meera steps up and enters the count into the crown's record under her own name, 'Meera of Kothi Shilak, called the Salt Fox,' as evidence of Varun's stolen-redbark trade. Asha testifies, and the button matches.
Rohan tells the assembly that the blockade killed Ranu's thirty-one and that he signed it.
Pritam is taken and Varun arrested. Meera's confession stays on the record.
Alone afterwards, Rohan says 'I love you' and holds up his bare hands: 'Watch my hands.' They stay warm (C20 payoff). She says it back, and her eight fingers stay warm.
Open-door scene in a borrowed room at Garh Neshar. What changes: love verified by the body, and she is held without counting anything.
His writ still orders him to deliver the Salt Fox at the thaw, and she has just confessed to being her.
chapters.reader_question_out: At the thaw, will he deliver her?
chapters.romance_change: Mutual declarations are verified by warm hands, and the threat line returns as devotion. Each makes a public self-incrimination for the other's cause.

chapters.title: The Winter Crossing Law
chapters.goal: Write a law that keeps the protection and ends the hanging.
chapters.value_shift: a broken law -> a drafted one
beats: Nimmi takes the two fingers. Rohan holds Meera's right hand, and she counts aloud while he counts with her.

They draft over the following weeks with Nimmi, Ila (who corrects every distance) and the hill council. The clauses: licensed bound guides, medicine always passes, and no one hangs for a death on a bound crossing. Rohan writes the last clause with Kiran in the room.
News: Varun goes to Taravan in chains when the passes open, Pritam is imprisoned, and 'the regent's general' has been exiled, though Ranu whispers otherwise (C24).

A warden can't pardon, so Rohan offers to name Meera on his writ as his guide for the return crossing. That enters her in the Closing Roll for life. She chooses it: 'I'll owe them winters. I'd give them anyway.'
Closed-door night. She asks him for something for herself for the first time: 'Stay.'
Meltwater weather comes, and they cross back over Shilak as a lawful pair to be at the cairn for the thaw.
chapters.reader_question_out: When the bond ends, what will they choose?
chapters.romance_change: She binds herself to the crown's roll beside him, and she asks for something for herself. Her need is met on the page.

chapters.title: First Thaw
chapters.goal: Be at the Shilak Cairn when the bond ends.
chapters.value_shift: bound by the mountain -> bound by choice; a book's peace -> a series threat
beats: At the cairn with Bindu, the Kothi villagers and Rohan's wardens, Meera hangs Jassi's goat bell on the stones (C25 payoff). She counts the drips from the snow cap.

Rohan's senior warden reminds him that the writ says deliver the Salt Fox at the thaw. Before the meltwater runs, Rohan says, 'I am not arresting her. I am walking to Taravan beside her, with the law in her hand.'
Meltwater runs at the cairn and the bond ends. She walks past eight arm-spans, feels no cold, and walks back.
They retie an ordinary rope of Bindu's new spinning by choice, and that is their betrothal. She calls him Rohan.

The stones ring. For the first time in living memory the jogini speak in the cold itself, and every hand at the cairn feels the words: the Old Bargain is unpaid, and the pass will close forever after the fourth winter unless someone pays.
Meera looks at the carved hands on the inner face. Rohan says Ila stayed in Neshar to finish her map, and that the queen will want it.
chapters.reader_question_out: What is the Old Bargain, and who will be made to pay?
chapters.romance_change: Free of the bond, they choose it again with an ordinary rope. She drops 'Captain' for his name: betrothal by choice.
